# GETGLOBAL

$\underline{\text { Problem 46798 }}$

In how many ways can three people be seated on a bench if two of them must sit next to each other?

## Solution

Let's consider one person sitting at the front (the first position). There is only one way for this person to sit there: either left or right from another seat. The second person will then also choose between these seats; thus, we get four possibilities - both persons could sit in any of the following positions:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \left(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{x} ; \mathrm{x}\right), \\
& \left(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{x}; \mathrm{x}\right) .
\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, the third person can sit in any of the remaining places as well, giving us six more options. Therefore, altogether there are eight different seating arrangements that satisfy our condition.

Answer: Eight ways.
